title: Strategy Ambassador: Towncall & OKR Slate
content:
Purpose

This doc captures a working slate of company-level Objectives and proposed Key Results (v0) that the Strategy Ambassador working group will present at the mid-March towncall. It also contains the proposed run of show for the towncall, suggested microslides + talking points for the exec segment, risk signals we want to surface, and a comms checklist for post-towncall follow-ups. This is an intentionally lightweight, editable draft for discussion with execs on 2025-03-04.

Context and framing (one-liner to open towncall)

Redwood’s next 90 days are focused on making inference predictable and economical for our customers while reducing per-token costs by engineering-first optimizations and tighter supply controls. We will measure success by throughput gains in Dedicated pools, reduction in per-token cost for hosted customers, and initial Private deployments with enterprise compliance checks in place.

Audience
- All employees (company towncall)
- Execs and managers (prep + Q&A)
- Customer-facing teams for follow-up comms (CS/solutions)

High-level towncall objectives (for the call itself)
- Align company on top 3 outcomes for the quarter.
- Present proposed company-level OKRs and where each org intersects.
- Surface biggest operational risks and mitigation commitments.
- Commit to 3 concrete customer and product experiments launching in next 60 days.

Proposed Company Objectives (v0)
- Objective A: Deliver industry-leading predictable inference economics
  - KR A1: Reduce average hosted text-generation cost per 1k tokens by 18% vs baseline (Jan 2025)
  - KR A2: Increase sustained throughput (p90 QPS) on Redwood Dedicated by 25% under standard batching profile
  - KR A3: Ship two quantization profiles in Redwood Optimize with verified <=2% quality delta on target benchmarks

- Objective B: Enterprise adoption and compliance readiness
  - KR B1: Complete 3 Private deployments (VPC or on-prem pilot) with enterprise audit logs enabled
  - KR B2: Close SOC2 gap items identified in the internal audit by end of quarter
  - KR B3: Convert two pilot customers to paid Dedicated contracts with 6+ month commits

- Objective C: Developer-first velocity and observability
  - KR C1: Reduce mean time to debug (tracing -> root cause) for production inference errors from 6h to <2h
  - KR C2: Increase adoption of per-route cost dashboards by 50% across paid customers
  - KR C3: Launch two SDK features requested by top PLG customers (streaming hooks, deterministic rollout flags)

Why these objectives (short rationale)
- Objective A maps directly to our thesis: serving economics drive product-level defensibility. B and C reduce sales friction and increase operational durability. Each objective was chosen to be measurable and to force trade-offs (latency vs cost, throughput vs reliability).

Cross-org intersections (how teams contribute)
- Engineering (serving-runtime): primary owner for A1/A2, will provide a short tech demo (KV caching, batching profile improvements).
- Product (hosted/dedicated teams): define customer-facing SLAs, rollout plans for new quantization profiles.
- Console & Observability: dashboards and trace hooks for C1/C2.
- Solutions & CS: run pilots for Private deployments and capture conversion learnings for B3.
- Security & Compliance: SOC2 gap remediation plan and audit milestones.

Towncall run of show (30–40 minutes recommended)
1) Exec opening (CEO, 3 min): framing + north star metrics to watch.
2) Strategy Ambassador slate (Aisha, 7 min): present three objectives, two key results each, and a one-line ask for every function.
3) Tech demo (Tom, 6 min): micro-demo of batching + KV caching improvements showing p90 improvement in a synthetic test.
4) Customer snapshot (Renee, 4 min): pilot outcome from recent Private deploy — highlights and blockers.
5) Risk heatmap + mitigation commitments (Marco, 5 min): top 5 risk signals and who owns mitigations.
6) Live Q&A (10–15 min): curated questions from Slack pre-submitted, plus 1–2 live.

Microslides / talking points for each segment (sparse speaker notes)
- Strategy Ambassador (Aisha): "We have three measurable bets this quarter. Each bet forces us to choose: speed for customers, predictable costs, or enterprise readiness. We will prioritize cost reductions that do not regress quality beyond 2%."
- Tech demo (Tom): one slide with before/after p90 latency, token cost delta, and a 1-slide architecture sketch of batching + kernel selection path.
- Customer snapshot (Renee): one slide: pilot timeline, SLA expectations, remaining blockers (network config, KMS integration), next customer-facing milestone.
- Risk heatmap (Marco): one slide matrix (Operational / Product / GTM / Security) with 5 red-amber-green items.

Top risks to surface (short)
- Risk 1: Quality regressions after aggressive quantization — mitigation: gated canary with automated evals + rollback in Optimize. Owner: Research/Applied ML.
- Risk 2: Dedicated capacity shortage during burst window — mitigation: temporary routing to regional hosted pools + committed burst contracts. Owner: Platform Engineering.
- Risk 3: SOC2 remediation drift — mitigation: weekly gating checklist and exec review. Owner: Security & Compliance.
- Risk 4: Customer confusion on cost-savings messaging (PLG churn) — mitigation: clear sample dashboards + cost-savings playbook for CS. Owner: Developer Experience.

Decision points for execs in the meeting (explicit asks)
- Approve the three company objectives as the primary focus for the quarter (yes/no).
- Greenlight A1 quantization pilot to run on 5% of Hosted traffic (yes/no).
- Commit to the Dedicated burst funding window (ops approval).

Post-towncall comms checklist (who does what within 48h)
- Send towncall recap + slide deck to all (Owner: Exec Comms / Aisha).
- Publish canonical OKR doc in Confluence with owners and measurement approach (Owner: Product Ops).
- Kickoff cross-functional sprints for the quantization pilot (Owner: Eng-APPLIED-ML).
- Schedule SOC2 remediation weekly cadence and publish first milestone (Owner: Security).

Open questions (for next exec sync)
- What is the acceptable upper bound for per-token quality delta for each customer tier? (PLG vs Enterprise)
- How do we measure the long tail cost delta from caching across heterogeneous request patterns?
- What is the threshold for converting a Private pilot into Dedicated sale (revenue / months / reliability)?

Appendix: suggested short metrics dashboard for execs (to be included in slides)
- Top-line: Company MRR, New Dedicated ARR, Number of Private Pilots active
- Cost/perf: Hosted cost per 1k tokens (rolling 7d), p90 latency for standard 512-token profile, Dedicated pool throughput (tokens/sec)
- Reliability: Errors per 1M requests, Mean time to rollback, Avg KV cache hit rate

Notes to presenters (practical)
- Keep slides to 4–6 visuals. Use a consistent color for risk (red/orange/green).
- Pre-gather 6 top Slack questions by Friday 2025-02-28 and pick 3 for live Q&A.
- Rehearsal: 2025-03-03 09:30–10:00 PT (Aisha, Tom, Renee, Marco).

Action items (immediate)
- Aisha: finalize OKR wording and owners by 2025-02-28 (in progress).
- Tom: record 90s demo clip for tech segment by 2025-03-01.
- Renee: permissioned customer slide + pilot permission to publish by 2025-02-27.
- Marco: risk heatmap draft and mitigation owners by 2025-02-26.

History/footnote
- Inspired by the Strategy Ambassador template used last year but condensed for a 30–40 minute towncall and with explicit asks to minimize follow-up ambiguity.

This doc is a living draft: please add suggestions inline or ping Aisha directly.
